assumptions: The drawing's two seat labels, 43 cm and 46 cm, are taken as seat depth 43 cm and seat width 46 cm, because the padded back above the seat is itself 43 cm wide and a seat is normally wider than its back. If they are the other way round the seat is 3 cm out in each direction.
The 6 cm label near the left arm is read as the armrest pad width, and the separate 6 cm label at the seat front is read as the seat cushion thickness.

The 11 cm label near the seat back could not be tied to a single edge; it is taken to dimension the back support upright behind the cushion (seat surface to bottom of the back pad). It is not used as a primary dimension for any part.
Back cushion thickness is assumed equal to the seat cushion thickness (6 cm) at low confidence and is raised as a blocking question.
Floor to the top of the base hub is assumed to be about 22 cm; this is what makes the 41 - 51 cm seat height range consistent with a 19 - 29 cm gas lift.
Castor wheels are assumed 5 cm diameter, typical for a chair with a 62 cm base span.
Seat deck, mechanism plate, hub and spoke sections are not visible in the drawing and are estimated inside normal ranges for this class of chair.
The five spokes are drawn tapering and swept downward; they are modelled as straight constant-section boxes for simplicity.
Twin-wheel castors are modelled as a single wheel cylinder plus a fork; the second wheel of each castor is not listed separately.
All upholstery is assumed to be polyester fabric over moulded foam; the drawing is line art with no material callout.
Maximum user weight of 130 kg and the +/- 2 cm tolerance noted on the sheet are recorded but do not affect part geometry.

joints.notes: Each arm loop bolts up into the underside of the seat deck through the mechanism plate.
Pad screws down onto the top of the arm loop; screwed rather than glued so the pad can be replaced.
Back frame fixed to the seat deck / mechanism with bolts through a bracket.
Back pad screwed through the shell onto the support; some chairs use clips, screws assumed.
Seat pad fixed down onto the deck with screws or clips.
Mechanism plate bolted to the underside of the seat deck.
Lever paddle clips into the mechanism housing.
Taper of the gas spring pressed into the taper socket of the mechanism.
Gas spring pressed into the moulded hub of the five-star base.
Spokes joined to the hub. If the base is moulded nylon rather than steel these are moulded integrally - material recorded as nylon, so treat as a one-piece joint.
Castor stem pushes into the socket at the end of each spoke.
Wheel on a rivet/axle through the fork.

missing_dimensions.question: How thick is the padded back of the chair, measured at its edge where it is not squashed?
missing_dimensions.why_needed: The back pad is modelled as a cushion, which needs a thickness as well as a width and height, or it cannot be generated at all.

missing_dimensions.question: How thick is the armrest pad - the distance through the soft pad on top of the arm, top to bottom?
missing_dimensions.why_needed: The arm pad is a cushion primitive and needs a thickness before it can be built; only its length and width are labelled.

missing_dimensions.question: How wide is the vertical gas-lift post under the seat, measured across the black column just above the star base?
missing_dimensions.why_needed: A cylinder needs a diameter and a length; the drawing gives neither, so the post cannot be modelled.

missing_dimensions.question: How wide is the centre block of the five-star base, measured across the middle where the five legs meet?
missing_dimensions.why_needed: The hub is the cylinder at the middle of the base and cannot be generated without a diameter and a height.

missing_dimensions.question: How tall is one castor wheel from the floor to the top of the wheel, not counting the metal fork above it?
missing_dimensions.why_needed: The castors set the height of the whole base; without a wheel diameter the floor-to-seat heights in the drawing cannot be reconciled with the geometry.

missing_dimensions.question: Looking from behind the chair, how wide is the rigid back frame that the padded back is fixed to, at its widest point?
missing_dimensions.why_needed: The back frame is a box and needs a width, height and depth; only the pad in front of it is dimensioned in the drawing.

missing_dimensions.question: How thick is the arm loop - the bar that runs from the seat up to the armrest? Measure across the bar itself.
missing_dimensions.why_needed: The arm bracket is modelled as a tube, which needs a section diameter as well as its 19 cm height.

missing_dimensions.question: How thick is the seat pan under the cushion, measured at the front edge of the seat just below the padding?
missing_dimensions.why_needed: This is the panel that the arms, back and gas lift all attach to; a default of 2 cm is assumed but it controls how low the cushion sits.

object.style_notes: Modern lightweight task chair drawn in a single line-art elevation with a part callout. Softly rounded upholstered back and seat, slim loop arms with oval pads, black nylon five-star base on twin-wheel castors, height adjustable on a gas spring with a lever under the seat. Drawing states a manufacturing tolerance of +/- 2 cm and a maximum user weight of 130 kg.
object.subtype: swivel task/office chair with arms, gas lift and five-star castor base

readability.notes: Single clean line drawing with printed dimension labels; all the main labels are legible. Weak points: (1) the two seat labels 43 cm and 46 cm sit on near-parallel diagonals and cannot be told apart with certainty, so the width/depth assignment is an assumption; (2) the 11 cm label sits in a cluttered area behind the seat and its leader does not clearly land on one edge; (3) the second 6 cm label points at the arm rather than an edge, so it is read as pad width; (4) no diameters at all are given for the gas lift, hub or castors, and nothing at all is shown of the underside of the seat.
